sections.subtitle: Word, character, and subword tokens
sections.description:
Word tokens are intuitive but explode in size. Character tokens are tiny but produce long sequences. Subword tokenization sits in between.

Byte-pair encoding learns frequent character pairs and merges them into tokens.

sections.subtitle: A tiny tokenizer
sections.description: Real tokenizers are trained on a corpus and shipped as a vocabulary plus merge rules. This example only shows the idea.

consoleBlock.py:
text = "AI learning hub is unbelievable"

print("words:", text.split())
print("characters:", list(text.replace(" ", "")))
print("lowercase:", text.lower().split())

sections.subtitle: Why BPE wins
sections.description:
BPE keeps common words intact and breaks rare words into reusable pieces. That gives a bounded vocabulary without losing the ability to represent new text.

It also means token counts are not word counts. Always measure with the tokenizer you actually use.
